subject: Customer latency spike — incident-time logs & evidence requests
messages:
From: Sam Williams <sam.williams@nimbus.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Latency spike impacting /v1/generate on high-volume customers

Jonas,

We hit a serious latency spike on our integration this morning between 08:45–09:05 PDT. Error rate for the streaming endpoint spiked to ~12% and p95 latency rose to ~1.8s (baseline ~220ms) — we had timeouts on several customer requests. Attaching a short KPI snapshot and a screenshot from our telemetry.

This is impacting two of our largest merchants; they're asking for what logs/evidence Redwood can provide for their incident review and for our execs. They specifically want:
- Per-request timestamps and error classification (HTTP codes / internal error tags) for the 20-minute window
- Any truncated/partial responses and whether user input was persisted in logs
- Confirmation of retention/erasure behavior for request bodies during incident handling

Can you confirm we can pull the above quickly and what the SLT-ready artifacts look like?

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Williams
Head of Integrations — Nimbus Payments

Attachments: nimbus_error_screenshot.png, incident_kpi_snapshot.csv

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Sam Williams <sam.williams@nimbus.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-08T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Latency spike impacting /v1/generate on high-volume customers

Sam — thanks for the heads up and the snapshots. I'm escalating immediately.

Quick answers up front: yes, we can provide per-request timing and error classification exports for that window; we also have a redacted access log and a tokenized request export option for compliance-sensitive customers. We need to coordinate on exactly how much PII/sample payload to include for the SLT bundle.

Internal ask (cc'd): Monica + Rishi, can you pull the following and tell Sam ETA?
- Full per-request logs (timestamps, route, model variant, error tags) for 08:30–09:10 PDT
- KV cache hit stats and batching behavior summary for the timeframe
- An export of the redwood-inference audit trace for the same window (session IDs + latency per hop)

Sam, we'll aim to deliver a packaged artifact (redacted for production PII) and a short incident write-up. If Nimbus needs full unredacted payloads we will need an executed DPA amendment or explicit approval from your security team — happy to expedite.

I'll coordinate a short exec-brief after we have the artifacts.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

From: monica_patel@redwood.com
To: Sam Williams <sam.williams@nimbus.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-08T09:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Latency spike impacting /v1/generate on high-volume customers

Sam / Jonas — tagging in next steps from customer ops:

What we'll provide in the first package (ETA ~90 minutes):
- CSV export of request/response metadata (no full request bodies) for 08:30–09:10 PDT
- Error breakdown (HTTP/5xx, model-timeouts, stream resets) with counts and sample IDs
- Aggregated latency distributions (p50/p90/p95) and a short note on contributing factors (observed batching burst + transient GPU scheduler throttling)

If Nimbus requires deeper payload-level proofs (forensics), we can provide a time-limited log-export (log-export-20260708.tar.gz). That package contains raw request IDs and timestamps; access will be gated and we will document handling steps.

One operational note: our default retention for request bodies is 30 days (configurable at the account level). Audit logs (metadata & access traces) are retained for 12 months. We will include the retention statements in the SLT bundle.

Laura — FYI for renewal/contract implications; may need to brief the customer success lead.

Thanks,
Monica
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-08T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Latency spike impacting /v1/generate on high-volume customers

Internal diagnostics update (for packaging):
- Collected per-request metadata export (IDs, timestamps, route, model variant, status codes) for 08:28–09:08 PDT. Output: incident_kpi_snapshot.csv + request_meta_08_28_09_08.csv (will include IDs only, not bodies).
- Gathered GPU telemetry and scheduler logs — these indicate a burst of concurrent small requests that increased batching latency briefly.
- Preparing an audit trace (redwood-audit-trace-20260708.json) that shows who accessed the exports and when — will redact user identifiers per the data handling SOP.

ETA: initial package to Sam by 10:45 PDT (CSV + short narrative). If Nimbus requests raw payloads we need signed approval; I'll prepare a Docusign request and a locked S3 export with short-lived credentials.

Attachments referenced: log-export-20260708.tar.gz (stub), redwood-audit-trace-20260708-summary.txt

Rishi Malhotra
Technical Support Lead, Redwood Inference

From: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
To: Sam Williams <sam.williams@nimbus.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-08T11:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Latency spike impacting /v1/generate on high-volume customers

Sam — thank you for escalating. A few security / evidence-handling clarifications to set expectations for your execs:

1) What we will include in the standard SLT bundle:
   - Metadata exports (timestamps, request IDs, status codes, model_variant) — can be provided immediately.
   - Access logs and audit trace showing our internal accesses to the artifacts (redacted).
   - A redacted SOC2 summary that highlights controls in place at the time of the incident (attached: redwood-soc2-summary-redacted.pdf).

2) What requires explicit customer approval or legal amendment:
   - Full request bodies / complete payloads containing customer PII: we will only release these after a signed DPA amendment or a scoped data-release authorization from your security team. The process is fast (typically DocuSign + short SOW) but it's gated by compliance.
   - Any raw logs that contain downstream customer identifiers linked to transactions — we will provide a redacted view by default.

3) Auditability & chain-of-custody:
   - All exported artifacts will have an access manifest and will be stored in a time-limited S3 export (short-lived creds). We will record who downloaded what and include that in the bundle.

Next steps:
- We'll publish the first SLT bundle (metadata CSV + narrative + SOC2 summary) to the linked Drive folder and notify your team.
- If Nimbus wants payload-level forensics, please confirm contact at your security team (name + email) so we can issue the DocuSign authorization and prepare the locked export.
- If your execs prefer a 15–20m incident briefing, I'm available at 1:00pm PDT today.

Evelyn Hart
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
Contact: evelyn.hart@redwood.com
